text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Add a two-stage auto-apply layer after PR-Agent: first, run a formatting-only bot (e.g., Prettier) on every PR; second, run a dependency-only bot (e.g., Renovate) on the repo weekly. Formatting is safe, fast, and avoids merge conflicts—trade-off is extra CI minutes. Dependency updates are riskier but prevent drift—trade-off is occasional bad pins. This keeps human review focused on real logic while automating the rest.

name: Gauge
text: Dependency bumps aren’t just risky—they’re a footgun when auto-applied blindly. The real risk isn’t merge conflicts; it’s breaking changes in minor/patch versions that silently fail tests or introduce security flaws. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* patch updates that pass CI, then require human review for minor/major bumps—trade-off is slower updates but fewer outages. Settle it by running a controlled experiment: apply patch-only bots to a staging repo for a month and measure failure rates vs. Renovate’s full-auto approach.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do this: Auto-apply *only* patch-level dependency updates that pass CI, with no human review. This cuts risk to near-zero while still saving time on trivial fixes. The trade-off is missing minor-version improvements that could bring features or security backports, but those rarely justify the blast radius.

name: Gauge
text: Patch-only auto-apply still misses the real blast radius: silent breaking changes in *patch* versions that CI doesn’t catch—think transitive deps, runtime env quirks, or security patches that expose new attack surfaces. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* security patches with a curated allowlist, then route all others to human review; this trades speed for safety where it matters most. Settle it by running a controlled experiment: compare patch-only auto-apply against security-only auto-apply with a 30-day failure rate metric.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Auto-apply *only* formatting tweaks immediately; route dependency bumps and all PRs through human review.

Result must deliver: a clear rule for what changes get auto-fixed versus what needs human sign-off, with CI configured to enforce it. Owned by Gauge.
